monitor.noLossData: Loss data will appear after training begins
monitor.diagnosticInsufficientSummary: At least 6 valid Loss points are required to assess the recent trend.
monitor.diagnosticConvergingSummary: The recent training Loss mean keeps falling, so the optimization objective is still improving.
monitor.diagnosticPlateauSummary: Recent movement is small and controlled; Loss may be entering a plateau.
monitor.diagnosticReboundSummary: The recent Loss mean is clearly above the previous window.
monitor.diagnosticVolatileSummary: Recent Loss dispersion is elevated and training stability needs attention.
monitor.diagnosticSteadySummary: Recent volatility is controlled, but improvement is not yet significant.
monitor.diagnosticInsufficientAdvice: Diagnostics update automatically as Loss data arrives.
monitor.diagnosticConvergingAdvice: Continue with the current setup and use fixed-prompt samples to verify actual quality changes.
monitor.diagnosticPlateauAdvice: Use sample quality to decide whether to continue; open TensorBoard for details.
monitor.diagnosticReboundAdvice: Observe the next epoch first; if it persists, inspect learning rate and data.
monitor.diagnosticVolatileAdvice: Check learning rate, batch size, and outlier samples before acting on a single point.
monitor.diagnosticSteadyAdvice: Keep watching sample quality and the next diagnostic window.
monitor.diagnosticEvidenceInsufficient: {count} valid points are available; at least {minimum} are required to compare two adjacent windows.
monitor.diagnosticEvidenceConverging: The recent window mean fell {magnitude}, meeting the ≤ -{converging}% decrease rule; volatility {volatility} remains below the {volatile}% alert threshold.
monitor.diagnosticEvidencePlateau: Absolute mean change {magnitude} is < {plateauChange}% and volatility {volatility} is < {plateauVolatility}%, meeting the plateau rule.
monitor.diagnosticEvidenceRebound: The recent window mean rose {magnitude}, meeting the ≥ +{rebound}% rebound rule; rebound has first priority.
monitor.diagnosticEvidenceVolatile: Recent coefficient of variation {volatility} meets the ≥ {volatile}% alert rule; mean change is {change}.
monitor.diagnosticEvidenceSteady: Mean change {change} and volatility {volatility} match none of the decrease, rebound, high-volatility, or plateau rules.
monitor.diagnosticWindowEvidence: Step {recentStart}–{recentEnd} vs Step {previousStart}–{previousEnd} · {window} points per window
monitor.diagnosticWindowPending: Waiting to form two adjacent statistical windows
monitor.diagnosticMethodMeta: Engineering alert · not a quality score
monitor.diagnosticScopeText: This only analyzes training Loss, not sample images or validation Loss. It cannot determine image quality, overfitting, or the best checkpoint, and never stops training automatically.
monitor.diagnosticMethodSourceText: Prefers TensorBoard loss/average (the trainer moving average, typically covering about one epoch); falls back to noisier loss/current when unavailable.
monitor.diagnosticMethodWindowText: Compares means from two adjacent equal windows. Target size is 15% of points, clamped to 12–60; short series use half the available points per window.
monitor.diagnosticMethodVolatilityText: Recent-window standard deviation divided by the absolute recent mean. It measures relative noise, not output quality.
monitor.diagnosticMethodNote: Long histories may be display-downsampled. Open TensorBoard for the complete curve, zooming, and point-level inspection.

stepEstimate.bucketFormula: {samples} samples go into {buckets} size buckets; split each bucket by Batch {batch} = {batches} batches/epoch
stepEstimate.epochFormula: Batch {batch} × accumulation {accumulation} = effective Batch {effectiveBatch}; per epoch: ⌈{batches} batches ÷ accumulation {accumulation}⌉ = {steps} steps
stepEstimate.epochFormulaMultiGpu: Batch {batch} × accumulation {accumulation} × {gpus} GPUs = effective Batch {effectiveBatch}; per epoch: ⌈{batches} batches ÷ {gpus} GPUs ÷ accumulation {accumulation}⌉ = {steps} steps
stepEstimate.sdScriptsNote: Uses the same bucket and ceiling rules as sd-scripts; recalculated before training starts.

field.vae_anima: VAE model file path (required for Anima - must use QwenImage VAE)
field.vae_sdxl: VAE model file path (optional for SD/SDXL)
field.krea_ditHint: Krea 2 DiT weights required by musubi-tuner
field.krea_vaeHint: Krea 2 VAE weights required by musubi-tuner
field.krea_text_encoderHint: Krea 2 uses a separate text encoder; it is required for both caching and training
field.krea_dataset_cache_dirHint: Always stored in .krea2-cache below the training data directory. Changing that directory updates the cache location. Prepare it again after images, captions, or models change
field.krea_resolutionHint: Krea 2 resolution must be positive multiples of 16, in width,height format
field.krea_network_argsHint: One key=value per line, passed directly as musubi --network_args
field.krea_optimizer_weight_decayHint: Leave empty for the selected optimizer's own default; a value is passed as musubi optimizer_args.
field.krea_optimizer_betasHint: Enter two or three comma-separated values, such as 0.9, 0.999. Supported lengths depend on the optimizer.
field.krea_optimizer_epsHint: Leave empty for the selected optimizer's default; a value is passed to musubi as a Python number.
field.krea_schedulefree_warmup_stepsHint: Passed to AdamWScheduleFree as warmup_steps; it does not use an external LR scheduler.
field.krea_adafactor_relative_stepHint: When enabled, AdaFactor computes its own LR and takes over scheduling. Disable it to use an external scheduler.
field.krea_adafactor_warmup_initHint: Only applies in relative-step mode; AdaFactor performs the warmup internally.
field.krea_lr_scheduler_internalLocked: The selected optimizer manages its own learning rate; the external scheduler is fixed to constant.
field.krea_lr_scheduler_timescaleHint: Leave empty for musubi to use the warmup steps. Only used by inverse_sqrt.
field.krea_lr_scheduler_min_lr_ratioHint: A 0–1 ratio of the initial LR. Used only by schedulers with a minimum-LR option.
field.krea_blocks_to_swap: Krea 2 DiT blocks swapped to CPU
field.krea_fp8_base: Load Krea 2 base model in FP8
field.krea_fp8_scaled: Enable scaled FP8 for Krea 2 (required with FP8 base)
field.krea_gradient_checkpointing_cpu_offloadH: Only works with gradient checkpointing; lowers VRAM further at a speed cost.
field.krea_ratio_or_stepsHint: Use a whole number of steps, or a ratio below 1 (for example 0.1 means 10% of total steps).
field.krea_use_pinned_memory_for_block_swap: Use pinned memory for Krea 2 block swap
field.krea_use_pinned_memory_for_block_swapHin: Can speed up CPU-to-GPU transfers; on Windows it uses more shared GPU memory.
field.krea_block_swap_h2d_onlyHint: Avoids backward D2H transfers; training requires gradient checkpointing and cannot use Turbo sampling.
field.enable_krea_samplesHint: Samples are written to the run's output/sample directory and temporarily load the text encoder at training start.
field.krea_sample_promptsHint: Each line may include musubi flags, e.g. A fox in snow. --w 1024 --h 1024 --s 8 --l 1 --d 0. Turbo recommends --l 1 --s 8.
field.krea_turbo_ditHint: RAW training with Turbo samples is recommended. Turbo cannot be combined with blocks_to_swap; leave empty to sample on RAW.
field.krea_turbo_dit_cache: Keep Turbo DiT resident in CPU memory
field.krea_turbo_dit_cacheHint: Faster samples, but uses roughly one additional DiT's worth of CPU RAM for the run.
field.resolution: Training image resolution in width,height format; non-square sizes are supported
field.resolutionHint: Anima: multiple of 16; SDXL: multiple of 64
field.enable_bucket: Enable ARB bucketing for non-square aspect ratios
field.bucket_no_upscale: Do not upscale images in buckets
field.bucket_reso_steps: ARB bucket resolution step (must be a multiple of the model's min step: Anima 16 / SDXL 64)
field.save_every_n_stepsHint: Independent of epoch saves. Recommended for large datasets
field.save_state: Save training state for resuming later
field.save_last_n_epochs_state: Only keep last N epochs of training state
field.train_batch_size: Images processed by each GPU at once; higher uses more VRAM and combines with accumulation to set the effective Batch
field.learning_rate: Overall learning rate. Effective for parts without a separate rate set
field.unet_lr: U-Net learning rate. Leave empty to use overall rate
field.text_encoder_lr: Text encoder learning rate. Leave empty to use overall rate
field.min_snr_gamma: Minimum SNR gamma. Recommended: 5 if enabled.
field.weight_decay: Weight decay. Leave empty for optimizer default.
field.weight_decayHint: Shows the selected optimizer's constructor default and merges into optimizer_args; unchanged defaults may be omitted.
field.stopcoefHint: EmoSens convergence threshold. Higher values trigger [READY TO STOP] earlier. Default: 0.04
field.prodigy_d0: Prodigy optimizer d0 parameter (initial D estimate, default 1e-6)
field.prodigy_safeguard_warmupHint: Enabled automatically with external LR warmup so warmup does not disturb the D estimate.
field.prodigyplus_use_stableadamwHint: Uses internal RMS update clipping by default; external max_grad_norm should be disabled while enabled.
field.schedulefree_warmup_stepsHint: Passed to AdamWScheduleFree as warmup_steps; external lr_warmup_steps has no effect for this optimizer.
field.adafactor_relative_stepHint: Enabled by default. AdaFactor computes the real LR from training steps and ignores LoRA+ group rates; disable it before enabling LoRA+.
field.adafactor_warmup_initHint: Only used with relative_step; warmup is then managed inside AdaFactor.
field.betasHint: Format: β1,β2. Leave empty for optimizer defaults. Adam: 0.9,0.999 | Lion: 0.9,0.99 | CAME: 0.9,0.999,0.9999
field.epsHint: Leave empty for the default: 1e-30 for Automagic3, usually 1e-8 otherwise
field.automagic_max_lrHint: A numerical-overflow guard, not a recommended training LR. The default 1e3 normally does not constrain adaptation; lower it only to impose a hard controller ceiling.
field.automagic_polarity_historyHint: Range 2–64; longer is steadier but slower to react
field.automagic_fusedLocked: Requires one GPU, gradient accumulation 1, max_grad_norm 0, and no fp16
field.emosensMultiGpuConflict: EmoSens conflict: gpu_ids is {value}; one GPU is required
field.came_eps1Hint: Small value for denominator stability. Default: 1e-30
field.optimizer_args_customHint: One key=value per line, passed to trainer's --optimizer_args
field.lr_warmup_steps_internalLocked: This optimizer manages LR internally and does not use external warmup
field.lr_scheduler_locked: This optimizer manages LR internally and does not use external LR scheduling
field.max_grad_norm_optimizerLocked: This optimizer configuration uses internal update clipping, so external max_grad_norm must be 0
field.learning_rate_prodigyLocked: Prodigy uses lr as a D-adaptation scaling factor, fixed at 1.0
field.unet_lr_prodigyLocked: Prodigy requires all learning rates at 1.0 (D-adaptation scaling), U-Net rate locked
field.text_encoder_lr_prodigyLocked: Prodigy requires all learning rates at 1.0 (D-adaptation scaling), text encoder rate locked
field.network_dim: Network dimension. Common range 4~128. Lower dim reduces VRAM.
field.network_alpha: Common values: equal to network_dim, or half, or 1.
field.network_dropout: Neuron dropout probability (drops neurons every step)
field.enable_loraplusHint: Uses native sd-scripts network_args to set regular and plus parameter-group rates; incompatible optimizer modes disable this toggle automatically.
field.enable_loraplus_optimizerLocked: The current optimizer mode cannot preserve LoRA+ group rates. Prodigy and EmoSens are unsupported; for AdaFactor, disable internal relative step first.
field.loraplus_lr_ratioHint: Default ratio for both UNet/DiT and text encoder; clear it to configure only one component
field.loraplus_unet_lr_ratioHint: Optional component override. Anima keeps the unet parameter name but applies it to the main DiT
field.loraplus_text_encoder_lr_ratioHint: Optional text-encoder override; use conservative ratios for few-shot character training
field.scale_weight_norms: Max norm regularization. Recommended: 1 if used.
field.network_args_customHint: One key=value per line. loraplus_* is managed by the LoRA+ toggle and ratio fields, so custom copies are ignored.
field.base_weightsHint: LoRA weight paths merged into the base model before training, comma-separated. Use to continue training on top of existing LoRAs
field.base_weights_multiplierHint: Merge multiplier per base_weights entry, comma-separated, must match count
field.keep_tokens: Keep first N tags from shuffle (requires shuffle_caption)
field.shuffle_caption: Shuffle tokens during training (unavailable when Anima caches TE outputs)
field.weighted_captions: Use weighted tokens (Anima unsupported; SDXL path only)
field.caption_dropout_rate: Probability of dropping all tags (still works under Anima caching)
field.caption_dropout_every_n_epochs: Drop all tags every N epochs
field.caption_tag_dropout_rate: Probability of dropping tags by comma (unavailable when Anima caches TE outputs)
field.sample_prompts: Positive prompt. What you want the preview to depict — tags or natural language.
field.negative_prompts: Negative prompt. What you do not want in the preview image.
field.mixed_precision: Training precision. RTX 30+ can use bf16.
field.full_bf16: Full BF16 training. Casts all model + network (LoRA) params to BF16. Eliminates dtype mismatches with torch.compile + LoRA. Only available when mixed_precision = bf16.
field.full_bf16_automagicLocked: Automagic3 compatibility mode requires FP32 LoRA trainable parameters; full_bf16 is disabled
field.cache_latents: Cache image latents to reduce VRAM
field.cache_text_encoder_outputs: Cache text encoder outputs to skip repeated encoding and speed up training
field.cache_text_encoder_outputs_to_disk: Cache text encoder outputs to disk
field.noise_offset: Noise offset for improving brightness and contrast
field.max_grad_norm: Global gradient clipping threshold (0=off; optimizer default or recommendation is shown)
field.timestep_sampling: Timestep distribution. sigmoid=σ(scaled normal), recommended; sigma=density sampling by weighting_scheme; uniform; shift=flow shift via discrete_flow_shift
field.sigmoid_scale: Scale for sigmoid/shift sampling; larger values concentrate at mid timesteps
field.discrete_flow_shift: FlowMatch schedule shift, effective with shift and sigma sampling (default 1.0)
field.weighting_scheme: Loss weighting. Density bias(logit_normal/mode) only under sigma sampling; Anima only weights sigma_sqrt/cosmap, others act as uniform
field.logit_mean: logit_normal density mean, requires sigma sampling
field.logit_std: logit_normal density std, requires sigma sampling
field.mode_scale: mode density scale, requires sigma sampling
field.min_timestepHint: Leave blank to use the default of 0
field.max_timestepHint: Leave blank to use the default of 1000
field.attn_mode: Attention implementation (Anima). torch=native; xformers=VRAM efficient; flash=fastest.
field.split_attn: Split attention computation (required with xformers, Anima)
field.vae_chunk_size: VAE spatial chunk size (even, Anima only)
field.vae_chunk_sizeHint: Reduces VRAM, leave empty to disable
field.blocks_to_swapHint: Offload DiT blocks to CPU to save VRAM. 0=no swap; Anima supports at most 8. Try 4~8 on low-VRAM GPUs.
field.conv_dim: Conv layer rank (LoCon / LoHa / LoKr: separate rank for 3x3 conv)
field.lokr_factor: LoKr factor (-1 = auto, smaller = fewer params)
field.lokr_factorHint: Common: 4~8. -1 = auto balance. Smaller = smaller file
field.use_tuckerHint: Decompose Conv2d kernel to reduce params for 3×3+ layers
field.use_scalar: Scalar output multiplier (LyCORIS only, smaller file)
field.rank_dropout: Rank dropout rate (drops whole ranks; stackable with neuron/module dropout)
field.module_dropout: Module dropout rate (drops whole modules; stackable with neuron/rank dropout)
field.lycoris_dropoutHint: Neuron dropout within LyCORIS modules; takes priority over network_dropout above if both set.
field.lycoris_preset: LyCORIS preset (target layers). Decides which network layers to train; default full. For DiT models (Anima) attn-mlp is recommended
field.dora_wdHint: Regularization via weight decomposition (alternative to dropout)
field.constraintHint: Recommended 0.1~1.0, effective only for OFT algorithms
field.rs_loraHint: Stabilizes low-rank training for LyCORIS LoCon
field.wd_on_outputHint: Only effective when DoRA (dora_wd) is on. Apply weight decomposition on the output dimension (default: on); turn off to use the input dimension instead.
field.torch_compile: Enable torch.compile (JIT compile for faster training)
field.torch_compileHint: Requires PyTorch 2.0+. First forward pass is slow (compilation warmup). On Windows, inductor backend may be unstable; switch to eager if errors occur.
field.dynamo_backendHint: inductor: default backend, highest optimization, may be unstable on Windows. eager: best compatibility, recommended for Windows and debugging. cudagraphs: uses CUDA Graph to reduce kernel launch overhead.
field.dim_from_weightsHint: Ignores network_dim; derives rank from existing LoRA weights
field.cuda_allow_tf32Hint: Nearly free 20~30% speedup on Ampere+ GPUs. Strongly recommended.
field.cuda_cudnn_benchmarkHint: Auto-picks fastest conv kernel at fixed resolution
field.vae_batch_sizeHint: Empty=default 1; larger speeds up caching but uses more VRAM
field.cpu_offload_checkpointingHint: Offload tensors to CPU during gradient checkpointing to save VRAM (U-Net/DiT). Incompatible with unsloth_offload_checkpointing or blocks_to_swap
field.unsloth_offload_checkpointingHint: Faster than cpu_offload_checkpointing; incompatible with blocks_to_swap
field.compileHint: Per-DiT-block compile speedup. Incompatible with blocks_to_swap. Windows: install VC++ Redist + triton-windows (one-click in Environment page)
field.persistent_data_loader_workersHint: Reduces inter-epoch wait; useful for large datasets, slightly more RAM
field.max_data_loader_n_workersHint: Empty=default 8; lower saves RAM, higher speeds loading
field.save_last_n_epochsHint: Pairs with save_every_n_epochs to avoid disk overflow; empty=no limit
field.save_state_on_train_end: Save state only at training end
field.noise_offsetHint: 0.1 is recommended; leave blank to disable
field.min_snr_gammaHint: Down-weights high-loss timesteps; paper recommends 5. Empty=off
field.multires_noise_iterationsHint: Multires (pyramid) noise iterations; recommend 6-10. SDXL only; Anima uses rectified-flow and ignores this.
field.multires_noise_discountHint: Multires noise discount; only effective when 'Multires noise iterations' is enabled. Default 0.3 is metadata-only when iterations not set.
field.ip_noise_gamma: Input perturbation noise gamma (regularization; effective for Anima at noising)
field.ip_noise_gamma_random_strength: Random strength for input perturbation noise
field.cache_text_encoder_outputsHint: Incompatible with caption shuffle and tag dropout; enabling either disables this cache
field.cache_text_encoder_outputsLocked: Caption shuffle / tag dropout is enabled, which is incompatible with caching. Turn off the relevant caption option to unlock
field.network_dropoutHint: Applies to all native modules (lora / lora_anima / loha / lokr). For LyCORIS, shares the same slot as the dedicated Dropout below; the dedicated one takes priority if set.
field.scale_weight_normsHint: Usually empty; set 1 for max-norm regularization when overfitting
field.sample_at_first: Generate a preview before training starts
field.sample_flow_shiftHint: Time-shift for Anima flow-match sampling (akin to Karras shift), default 3.0. Anima only; SDXL ignores it.
field.samplePromptsCountHint: {n} prompt lines → {n} preview images per sample

opt.save_precision_fp16: Half-precision float (16-bit), small file size, recommended
opt.save_precision_bf16: Brain Float 16, wider numeric range, suitable for training
opt.save_precision_float: Full-precision float (32-bit), largest file but highest precision
opt.lr_scheduler_cosine_with_restarts: Cosine annealing with periodic restarts, recommended for most training
opt.lr_scheduler_cosine: Cosine annealing, smoothly reduces learning rate
opt.optimizer_type_AdamW: Standard AdamW optimizer, higher VRAM usage
opt.optimizer_type_AdamW8bit: 8-bit AdamW, saves VRAM, recommended for general training
opt.optimizer_type_PagedAdamW8bit: Paged 8-bit AdamW, for tight VRAM scenarios
opt.optimizer_type_Lion: Lion optimizer (EvoLved Sign Momentum), fast convergence
opt.optimizer_type_Prodigy: Adaptive learning rate optimizer, auto-tunes LR, recommended for beginners
opt.optimizer_type_ProdigyPlus: ProdigyPlus + Schedule-Free, dual automation: no LR or scheduler tuning needed
opt.optimizer_type_Automagic3: Experimental adaptive-LR optimizer using compatibility mode by default
opt.optimizer_type_AdamWScheduleFree: AdamW + Schedule-Free, no learning rate scheduler needed
opt.krea_optimizer_adamw8bit: The 8-bit AdamW used in musubi's Krea 2 example; usually the VRAM-friendly default.
opt.krea_optimizer_adamw: Standard PyTorch AdamW without 8-bit optimizer states.
opt.krea_optimizer_adafactor: AdaFactor supported directly by musubi; relative-step mode manages LR inside the optimizer.
opt.krea_optimizer_paged_adamw8bit: Paged 8-bit AdamW; useful to try under severe VRAM pressure.
opt.krea_optimizer_ademamix8bit: bitsandbytes AdEMAMix 8-bit implementation with its three betas exposed as guided controls.
opt.krea_optimizer_lion8bit: bitsandbytes 8-bit Lion; its typical LR is higher than Adam-family settings.
opt.krea_optimizer_came: CAME from pytorch_optimizer, already present in the shared sd-scripts training environment.
opt.krea_optimizer_lion: Lion from pytorch_optimizer, already present in the shared training environment.
opt.krea_optimizer_prodigy: D-adaptation optimizer from prodigyopt; the initial LR is suggested as 1.0.
opt.krea_optimizer_schedulefree: AdamW from schedulefree; musubi uses its internal LR logic and skips an external scheduler.
opt.krea_optimizer_torch_sgd: Standard PyTorch SGD without momentum by default; arbitrary custom parameters are not exposed for Krea 2.
opt.optimizer_type_EmoSens: EmoSens: emotion-driven optimizer with automatic emoPulse learning rates
opt.loss_type_default: Use the model's default loss function
opt.loss_type_l1: L1 Loss (MAE), more robust to outliers
opt.loss_type_l2: L2 Loss (MSE), more sensitive to large errors
opt.loss_type_huber: Huber Loss, combines advantages of L1 and L2
opt.loss_type_smooth_l1: Smooth L1 Loss, smoother near zero
opt.network_module_networks_lora: Standard LoRA network for SD/SDXL architectures
opt.network_module_networks_lora_anima: Anima LoRA network. Anima model is derived from NVIDIA Cosmos-Predict2-2B.
opt.network_module_lycoris_kohya: LyCORIS Library (DoRA, GLoRA, OFT, and more)
opt.lycoris_preset_full: All layers: all UNet/DiT modules + text encoder, includes convolution. Most parameters, strongest tuning, largest file. Default
opt.lycoris_preset_full_lin: All layers (no conv): all UNet/DiT linear modules + text encoder, no convolution. Smaller than full; little difference from full on DiT
opt.lycoris_preset_attn_mlp: Attention + MLP: only Transformer blocks (attention + MLP), no conv/ResnetBlock. DiT main layers, high value. Recommended
opt.lycoris_preset_attn_only: Attention only: only attention layers + text encoder attention. Fewest params, smallest file, light style tweaks
opt.lycoris_preset_unet_only: UNet/DiT only: all UNet/DiT modules + conv, no text encoder
opt.lycoris_preset_unet_transformer: UNet/DiT Transformer only: only DiT Transformer blocks, no conv, no text encoder. DiT slim version
opt.lycoris_preset_unet_convblock: UNet conv blocks only: only ResnetBlock2D/Downsample2D/Upsample2D + conv_in/conv_out. For traditional UNet (SD1.5/SDXL), mostly ineffective on DiT
opt.lycoris_preset_ia3: IA3 only: only to_k/to_v/ff.net.2 projection layers. Use only with IA3 algorithm
opt.sample_sampler_ddim: DDIM sampler, fast with stable output
opt.sample_sampler_euler_a: Euler Ancestral, fast sampler with randomness, recommended for previews
opt.mixed_precision_bf16: BFloat16 mixed precision, wide numeric range, recommended for BF16-capable GPUs
opt.mixed_precision_fp16: FP16 mixed precision, saves VRAM, compatible with older GPUs
opt.mixed_precision_no: No mixed precision (FP32), highest VRAM usage
opt.timestep_sampling_sigmoid: sigmoid — σ(scaled normal), recommended for Anima
opt.attn_mode_flash: Flash Attention, fastest but requires GPU support
opt.huber_schedule_snr: SNR-based dynamic schedule, adaptively adjusts Huber threshold
opt.dynamo_backend_inductor: Default backend, highest optimization, recommended for Linux/macOS
opt.dynamo_backend_eager: Best compatibility backend, recommended for Windows and debugging
opt.dynamo_backend_cudagraphs: Uses CUDA Graph to reduce kernel launch overhead
opt.timestep_sampling_flux_shift: Flux Shift (timestep distribution shift for Flux models)
opt.compile_backend_cudagraphs: Reduces kernel launch overhead via CUDA Graph
opt.compile_dynamic_true: Enable dynamic shapes (needs VS2022 C++ on Windows)
